ahead: The survey is done and written to lean/ERDOS-359-MATHLIB-SURVEY.md. Nothing stopped me. Three things the next attempt will hit. (1) The analysis half of Erdos 359 is essentially covered by Mathlib v4.33.0-rc2: IsEquivalent has full mul/div/inv/pow/congr arithmetic plus tendsto_atTop and comp_tendsto, and the nat-cast-to-atTop bridge (tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop, tendsto_natCast_atTop_iff) is there. The combinatorial half has NO support at all: grepping Mathlib for Sidon, sumFree, IsSumFree, mianChowla, greedy returns only unrelated hits in Linarith and Besicovitch. The cost of this problem is the counting argument, not the limits. (2) Nothing in the formal-conjectures statement asserts that a sequence satisfying IsGoodFor exists, and there is no DecidablePred instance for its IsLeast set, so all four theorems are currently vacuous-until-proved-otherwise. Build existence first. (3) Every statement divides by Real.log (Real.log k), which is NEGATIVE for k <= 15 and zero at k = e. The low-values variant (k <= 7) and the asymptotic variant therefore live on disjoint ranges and no single global positivity lemma covers both. Mathlib has exactly one file about iterated log (Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/InvLog.lean) and it exposes only Real.one_isLittleO_log_log, Real.deriv_log_log, Real.differentiableOn_log_log and non-continuity facts; log log x -> atTop is used inside a proof there but is not a named lemma. Also note ENNReal.limsup_const_mul / limsup_mul_le / eventually_le_limsup all require [CountableInterFilter f], which atTop on nat does not satisfy; only the ENNReal _of_ne_top family and the EReal lemmas are usable on atTop.

work.what:
Add a named Mathlib lemma for the divergence of the iterated real logarithm, and use it to simplify the existing proof of Real.one_isLittleO_log_log. Target statement, in Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/InvLog.lean, namespace Real, with `open Filter`:

    theorem tendsto_log_log_atTop : Tendsto (fun x => log (log x)) atTop atTop :=
      tendsto_log_atTop.comp tendsto_log_atTop

That exact composition already appears, unnamed, at line 132 of Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/InvLog.lean inside the proof of `Real.one_isLittleO_log_log`. Mathlib pin for this survey: v4.33.0-rc2. There is currently no `Real.tendsto_log_log_atTop` anywhere in Mathlib; a grep for declaration names matching log_log returns only deriv_log_log, deriv_log_log_apply, differentiableAt_log_log, differentiableOn_log_log, differentiableOn_log_log', hasDerivAt_log_log, not_continuousAt_log_log_zero, not_continuousAt_log_log_one, not_continuousAt_log_log_neg_one and one_isLittleO_log_log.

Add a named Mathlib lemma stating that the iterated logarithm is little-o of the logarithm. Target statement, in Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/InvLog.lean, namespace Real, with `open Filter Asymptotics`:

    theorem isLittleO_log_log_log : (fun x => log (log x)) =o[atTop] log

Proof sketch that should work on Mathlib v4.33.0-rc2: `Real.isLittleO_log_rpow_atTop (r := 1) one_pos : log =o[atTop] fun x => x ^ (1:ℝ)` (Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Asymptotics.lean:364), then `Asymptotics.IsLittleO.comp_tendsto` (Mathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/Defs.lean:444) along `Real.tendsto_log_atTop` (Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean:351), then rewrite with `Real.rpow_one`. No such lemma exists in Mathlib today.

Add a named Mathlib lemma giving eventual positivity of the iterated real logarithm, so that dividing by log (log x) on atTop is legal without a hand-rolled `have` at every call site. Target statement, in Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/InvLog.lean, namespace Real, with `open Filter`:

    theorem eventually_log_log_pos : Forall-eventually x in atTop, 0 < log (log x)

written in Lean as `theorem eventually_log_log_pos : ∀ᶠ x in atTop, 0 < Real.log (Real.log x)`. It follows from `Real.tendsto_log_log_atTop` (see the sibling work item; or inline `Real.tendsto_log_atTop.comp Real.tendsto_log_atTop`) via `Filter.Tendsto.eventually_gt_atTop 0`. This cannot be a global bound: log (log x) is negative for x < e^e ≈ 15.15 and undefined-as-junk below 1. Mathlib pin v4.33.0-rc2 has no such lemma.

Add the missing converse of Asymptotics.IsLittleO.of_tendsto_div_atTop to Mathlib. Mathlib v4.33.0-rc2 has, at Mathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/Lemmas.lean:444, in the section `div_tendsto_infty` with variables `{𝕜 : Type*} [NormedField 𝕜] [LinearOrder 𝕜] [IsStrictOrderedRing 𝕜] [OrderTopology 𝕜] {l : Filter α} {f g : α → 𝕜}`:

    theorem IsLittleO.of_tendsto_div_atTop (h : Tendsto (fun x ↦ g x / f x) l atTop) : f =o[l] g

but it has no lemma in the other direction. Target statement:

    theorem IsLittleO.tendsto_div_atTop (h : f =o[l] g) (hf : ∀ᶠ x in l, 0 < f x) :
        Tendsto (fun x ↦ g x / f x) l atTop

The eventual-positivity hypothesis (or eventual non-vanishing plus a sign condition) is necessary; without it the statement is false. This is the exact step needed to derive a statement of the shape `Tendsto (fun k ↦ (A k : ℝ) / k) atTop atTop` from an asymptotic equivalence for A, so it is on the critical path for Erdos problem 359 part (i).

Prove that the Erdos-359 greedy sequence exists and is unique, in Lean 4 / Mathlib (pin v4.33.0-rc2), and supply the decidability instance its defining set needs. The predicate, verbatim from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/359.lean, with `open Filter Asymptotics`:

    def IsGoodFor (A : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Prop := A 0 = n ∧ StrictMono A ∧
      ∀ j, IsLeast
        {m : ℕ | A j < m ∧ ∀ a b, Finset.Icc a b ⊆ Finset.Iic j → m ≠ ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc a b, A i}
        (A <| j + 1)

Three deliverables. (1) Existence: `theorem exists_isGoodFor (n : ℕ) : ∃ A, IsGoodFor A n`. Build A by Nat.rec, taking A (j+1) to be Nat.find applied to the nonemptiness proof of the displayed set; the nonemptiness comes from a pigeonhole count, see the sibling gap-bound work item. Useful Mathlib names, all verified present at that pin: Nat.isLeast_find (Mathlib/Order/Nat.lean:40), Set.Nonempty.isLeast_natFind (Mathlib/Order/Nat.lean:47), Nat.sInf_mem (Mathlib/Order/Lattice/Nat.lean:80), Nat.notMem_of_lt_sInf (:85), Nat.sInf_le (:91), strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ (Mathlib/Order/Monotone/Basic.lean:569). (2) Uniqueness: `theorem IsGoodFor.unique {A B : ℕ → ℕ} {n : ℕ} (hA : IsGoodFor A n) (hB : IsGoodFor B n) : A = B`, by induction on the index using IsLeast.unique (Mathlib/Order/Bounds/Basic.lean:830). (3) A DecidablePred instance for the membership predicate. The `∀ a b` quantifier is unbounded as written, so it must first be replaced by a bounded one: Finset.Icc a b ⊆ Finset.Iic j forces b ≤ j whenever a ≤ b, and Finset.Icc a b = ∅ when b < a (Finset.Icc_eq_empty_of_lt, Mathlib/Order/Interval/Finset/Basic.lean:114), in which case the sum is 0. Without (1) all four Erdos-359 theorems are vacuously about a predicate nothing is known to satisfy.

Prove the pigeonhole gap bound for the Erdos-359 greedy sequence in Lean 4 / Mathlib (pin v4.33.0-rc2). The sequence is characterised by, verbatim from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/359.lean:

    def IsGoodFor (A : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Prop := A 0 = n ∧ StrictMono A ∧
      ∀ j, IsLeast
        {m : ℕ | A j < m ∧ ∀ a b, Finset.Icc a b ⊆ Finset.Iic j → m ≠ ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc a b, A i}
        (A <| j + 1)

Deliverable: for A with IsGoodFor A 1, the number of distinct values expressible as ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc a b, A i with Finset.Icc a b ⊆ Finset.Iic j is at most (j+1)*(j+2)/2, hence some m with A j < m ≤ A j + (j+1)*(j+2)/2 + 1 is not so expressible, hence A (j+1) ≤ A j + (j+1)*(j+2)/2 + 1. This both witnesses nonemptiness of the IsLeast set (so it feeds existence) and gives the first nontrivial upper bound on growth. Mathlib names verified present at that pin and expected to carry the argument: Finset.card_image_le (Mathlib/Data/Finset/Card.lean:230), Finset.card_le_card (:66), Finset.exists_mem_notMem_of_card_lt_card (:614), Nat.card_Icc (Mathlib/Order/Interval/Finset/Nat.lean:83), Nat.card_Iic (:93), Finset.Icc_subset_Iic_self (Mathlib/Order/Interval/Finset/Basic.lean:439), Finset.sum_Icc_succ_top (to_additive image of Finset.prod_Icc_succ_top, Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Intervals.lean:74). Note that Mathlib has no Sidon-set, sum-free-set, or greedy-sequence infrastructure whatsoever: a grep over all of Mathlib for Sidon, sumFree, IsSumFree, mianChowla and greedy returns only unrelated hits in Linarith and Besicovitch. This argument has to be built from Finset cardinality lemmas by hand.

Prove the finite, non-open variant of Erdos problem 359 in Lean 4 / Mathlib (pin v4.33.0-rc2). Target, verbatim from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/359.lean, where IsGoodFor is as in the sibling existence work item:

    /-- Suppose monotone sequence $A$ satisfies the following: `A 0 = 1` and for all `j`, `A (j + 1)` is the
    smallest natural number that cannot be written as a sum of consecutive terms of `A 0, ..., A j`.
    Then the first few terms of $A$ are $1,2,4,5,8,10,14,15,...$. -/
    @[category test, AMS 11]
    theorem erdos_359.variants.isGoodFor_1_low_values (A : ℕ → ℕ) (hA : IsGoodFor A 1) :
        A '' (Set.Iic 7) = {1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 14, 15} := by
      sorry

This is the only one of the four statements in that file that is not an open research problem, so it is the natural first target. It is provable by eight applications of IsLeast.unique (Mathlib/Order/Bounds/Basic.lean:830) against explicitly computed candidate values, then Set.image_insert_eq (Mathlib/Data/Set/Image.lean:322) to unfold the image of Set.Iic 7. It does not need the existence theorem, only uniqueness of each successive term given hA.

edges.why: Existence of a sequence satisfying IsGoodFor requires the IsLeast set to be nonempty at every index, and the only route to that is the pigeonhole count in the gap-bound item: at most (j+1)(j+2)/2 values are expressible as sums of consecutive terms, so some value just above A j is not.
The low-values variant needs the uniqueness half (IsLeast.unique applied term by term) to pin A 0 through A 7 to specific numerals; without it the hypothesis constrains A but does not determine it.

Eventual positivity of log (log x) is the one-line consequence Tendsto.eventually_gt_atTop of the divergence lemma; landing the divergence lemma first keeps the positivity proof from re-deriving the composition inline.
